level.title: Korean A2+ — Bank and phone shop
goals: Open and use a bank account, and ask what a fee is for
Change a phone plan, a device or a carrier without losing the number
Report a lost card or a broken phone and ask for the fix

lessons.title: 통장을 만들어요
lessons.learn: Opening an account is a paperwork conversation: 통장을 만들고 싶어요, 신분증이 필요해요, 며칠 걸려요. The polite request takes -고 싶은데요.

grammar.title: Requests at the counter
grammar.pattern: 통장을 만들고 싶은데요 · 신분증이 필요해요 · 며칠 걸려요?
grammar.explain: -고 싶은데요 states what you came for and leaves the sentence open for the clerk to answer, which is the standard counter manner. Requirements take 이/가 필요하다.

examples.en: I would like to open an account.
Identification is required.
How many days does it take?

mistakes.why: One predicate: -고 싶은데요 already states the request.
필요하다 takes 이/가 on the thing needed.

dialogue.en: Hello, I would like to open an account.

dialogue.t: 네, 신분증이 필요합니다. 외국인 등록증 있으세요?
dialogue.r: ne, sinbunjeung-i piryohamnida. oegugin deungnokjeung isseuseyo?
dialogue.en: Yes, identification is required. Do you have an alien registration card?
Yes, here it is. How long does it take?

dialogue.t: 오늘 바로 됩니다. 비밀번호를 정해 주세요.
dialogue.r: oneul baro doemnida. bimilbeonho-reul jeonghae juseyo.
dialogue.en: It is done today. Please set a password.

lessons.title: 현금을 찾아요
lessons.learn: At the machine the verbs are 찾다 and 넣다, the password is 비밀번호, and the remaining balance is 잔액. A fee is 수수료 and it is always worth asking.

grammar.title: At the machine
grammar.pattern: 현금을 찾고 싶어요 · 잔액을 확인해 주세요 · 수수료가 얼마예요?
grammar.explain: 찾다 covers both looking for and withdrawing; the machine's screen offers to 확인하다 the balance. Money amounts are Sino-Korean and need a counter — 만 원, 오천 원.

examples.en: I would like to withdraw cash.
Please check the balance.
How much is the fee?

mistakes.why: Withdrawing and depositing are separate actions; state the one you want.
The amount already names the money — 돈 is not added after it.

dialogue.t: 현금을 찾고 싶은데 기계를 못 쓰겠어요.
dialogue.r: hyeongeum-eul chatgo sipeunde gigye-reul mot sseugesseoyo.
dialogue.en: I want to withdraw cash but I cannot work the machine.

dialogue.t: 괜찮습니다. 카드를 여기에 넣고 비밀번호를 누르세요.
dialogue.r: gwaenchanseumnida. kadeu-reul yeogi-e neoko bimilbeonho-reul nureuseyo.
dialogue.en: It is fine. Put the card here and enter your password.
How much is the fee?
At this bank's own machines it is free.

lessons.title: 해외로 송금해요
lessons.learn: A transfer needs the recipient, the bank code and the number of days: 받는 분, 은행 코드, 사흘쯤 걸려요. The amount that arrives differs from the amount sent.

grammar.title: Sending money abroad
grammar.pattern: 해외로 송금하고 싶어요 · 사흘쯤 걸려요 · 환율이 어떻게 돼요?
grammar.explain: 걸리다 takes the time as its subject: 사흘쯤 걸려요. A polite person-reference is 받는 분 rather than the plain 사람, and the rate is asked with 어떻게 돼요.

examples.en: I would like to send money abroad.
It usually takes about three days.
What is today's exchange rate?

mistakes.why: 걸리다 takes the duration without 을/를, and 쯤 softens it to about.
받는 분 already means the recipient politely; 사람 and 분 are not stacked.

dialogue.en: I would like to send money abroad.
Do you know the recipient's bank code?
Yes, here it is. How many days does it take?

dialogue.t: 보통 사흘쯤 걸리고, 환율은 오늘 기준입니다.
dialogue.r: botong saheul-jjeum geolligo, hwannyul-eun oneul gijun-imnida.
dialogue.en: Usually about three days, and the rate is today's.

lessons.title: 요금제를 바꿔요
lessons.learn: Plans are compared with 보다: 데이터가 더 많고 요금이 싸요. A contract runs for a fixed term, 약정, and leaving early costs money.

grammar.title: Comparing plans
grammar.pattern: 요금제를 바꾸고 싶어요 · 데이터가 더 많아요 · 약정이 남았어요
grammar.explain: Comparison takes 더 … than … with 보다 or a plain 더: 데이터가 더 많아요. A remaining contract is 남다, and the term itself is 약정, not 계약, in phone shops.

examples.en: I would like to change my plan.
This plan has more data.
A year is left on the contract.

mistakes.why: One predicate per sentence.
남다 already says that time remains.

dialogue.en: I would like to change my plan.
How many gigabytes is your current plan?

dialogue.t: 삼 기가예요. 더 많은 걸로 바꾸고 싶어요.
dialogue.r: sam giga-yeyo. deo manheun geollo bakkugo sipeoyo.
dialogue.en: Three gigabytes. I would like to change to a bigger one.

dialogue.t: 그럼 이 요금제가 좋아요. 다만 약정이 일 년 남았습니다.
dialogue.r: geureom i yogeumje-ga joayo. daman yakjeong-i il nyeon namatseumnida.
dialogue.en: Then this plan is good. Note that a year is left on your contract.

lessons.title: 번호를 옮겨요
lessons.learn: Keeping your number while changing carrier is 번호 이동. The old carrier must confirm there is no remaining contract, and the new one issues a SIM the same day.

grammar.title: Porting a number
grammar.pattern: 번호를 그대로 유지하고 싶어요 · 통신사를 바꿔도 돼요? · 오늘 바로 됩니다

examples.en: I would like to keep my number as it is.
May I change carrier?
The SIM is issued today.

mistakes.why: Porting keeps the number — 바꾸다 would mean a new number.

dialogue.r: ne, beonho idong-euro ganeunghamnida. yakjeong-i nama isseumyeon hwagin-i piryohaeyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, by porting. If a contract remains, confirmation is needed.

I will call the carrier and confirm it for you.

lessons.title: 카드를 잃어버렸어요
lessons.learn: A lost card is reported in one sentence and stopped immediately: 카드를 잃어버려서 정지시켜 주세요. A replacement is 재발급.

grammar.title: Reporting a loss
grammar.pattern: 카드를 잃어버렸어요 · 정지시켜 주세요 · 재발급을 신청하고 싶어요
grammar.explain: The loss is stated in the past and the request follows in the same breath; -아서/어서 links them. The card is the object of 정지시키다, and 신청하다 is the verb for applying.

examples.en: I have lost my card.
Please block it right away.
I would like to apply for a replacement.

mistakes.why: The accidental sense takes 잃어버리다, and it ends the clause.
정지시키다 takes 을/를 on the card.

dialogue.en: I have lost my card. Please block it right away.
Confirmed. The balance is safe. Would you like a replacement?
Yes. How long does it take?

dialogue.t: 일주일쯤 걸리고, 그동안 임시 카드를 쓸 수 있습니다.
dialogue.r: iljuil-jjeum geolligo, geudongan imsi kadeu-reul sseul su itseumnida.
dialogue.en: About a week; you can use a temporary card in the meantime.

culture.text: Korean banking and phone shops run on identification and paperwork. Opening an account needs 신분증 and often an 외국인 등록증; a phone plan is a contract with a fixed term, 약정, and the price of leaving early is stated plainly before you sign. Payments are overwhelmingly card and app rather than cash, and the machine asks for the card first and the password second. Because so much of daily life is tied to a phone number, porting it — 번호 이동 — is a routine transaction with its own vocabulary.

reading.text: 지난주에 은행에 갔습니다. 통장을 만들고 싶다고 말했더니 직원이 신분증을 요청했습니다. 서류를 쓰고 비밀번호를 정했습니다. 그다음에 현금을 찾으려고 기계에 갔는데 방법을 몰라서 직원에게 물었습니다. 같은 은행 기계는 수수료가 없었습니다. 오늘은 휴대폰 가게에도 갔습니다. 요금제를 바꾸고 번호는 그대로 유지했습니다. 생각보다 간단했습니다.
reading.gloss: Last week I went to the bank. When I said I wanted to open an account, the clerk asked for identification. I filled in the papers and set a password. Then I went to the machine to withdraw cash, but I did not know how, so I asked the clerk. At the bank's own machines there was no fee. Today I also went to the phone shop. I changed the plan and kept my number as it was. It was simpler than I expected.

listening.script:
직원: 어떻게 도와드릴까요?
지훈: 카드를 잃어버려서 정지시키고 싶어요.
직원: 언제 잃어버리셨어요?
지훈: 어제 저녁에요. 그리고 재발급도 신청하고 싶어요.
직원: 알겠습니다. 재발급은 일주일쯤 걸립니다.
지훈: 그동안 카드 없이 쓸 수 있어요?
직원: 휴대폰 결제를 쓰시면 됩니다.
listening.gloss: Clerk: How can I help? Jihun: I have lost my card and would like to block it. Clerk: When did you lose it? Jihun: Yesterday evening. And I would like to apply for a replacement too. Clerk: Understood. A replacement takes about a week. Jihun: Can I manage without a card meanwhile? Clerk: You can use phone payment.

task.instructions: Write two short dialogues: one at a bank about a lost card, one at a phone shop about a repair. Each needs the problem in one sentence, a request with -아/어 주세요, one question about time or cost, and a closing line from the staff.
